newsitem.title: MEXICO: Moderna up sharply on B.A.T deal.
newsitem.headline: Moderna up sharply on B.A.T deal.

text.p: Shares in Mexican conglomerate Empresas La Moderna (ELM) were up sharply in early trade following news it had sold a 50 percent stake in its cigarette division, traders and analysts said.
Moderna A shares surged 3.30 pesos to 47.70 pesos in brisk trade in Mexico City, while their ADRs jumped 1-1/4 to 23-3/4 in New York.
"Foreigners have stepped in to buy Moderna, it's underpriced," a desk trader said.
Francisco Chavez, an analyst at Smith Barney said B.A.T Industries had paid the equivalent of more than $30 per ADR for the cigarette division alone.
"It looks like ELM got a really good price, especially when you compare it to what Grupo Carso got for selling a stake in Cigatam," Chavez said.
ELM said Tuesday it had reached an agreement to sell a controlling 50 percent interest in its cigarette division Cigarrera La Moderna (CLM) to B.A.T Industries for $1.712 billion.
B.A.T Industries had also obtained an option to buy all remaining shares in CLM.
